faqs.q: What should I include on an HVAC estimate?
faqs.a: At minimum: your business name and license number, the client and job-site address, dated line items (diagnostic, repair, replacement or maintenance), a valid-until date, deposit terms and exclusions. Most states require an HVAC contractor license on client-facing documents.

faqs.q: Is this template free to use?
faqs.a: Yes. All three formats (PDF, Word, Excel) are free to download with no email required.

faqs.q: Does the Excel version calculate the deposit and balance automatically?
faqs.a: Yes. Enter your quantity and rate per line, and the subtotal, 30% deposit and balance due update automatically.

faqs.q: Can I use this as an HVAC quote template?
faqs.a: Yes. An HVAC quote and an HVAC estimate are the same document - a written price for proposed work before the job starts. This template includes common HVAC line items (installation, equipment, labor, permits) and is valid as a quote. Enter your quantities and rates, total the job, and present it to the client for approval.

faqs.q: Is this suitable as an HVAC price list template?
faqs.a: Yes. The line-item structure of this HVAC estimate template works as a price list - list each service (tune-up, capacitor, refrigerant, installation) with its unit price. Clients can see exactly what each item costs. Use the Excel version so prices auto-total when quantities are entered.

faqs.q: Is this legal or tax advice?
faqs.a: No. Templates are for informational purposes only. Requirements vary by state — verify with your licensing board and a CPA or attorney before use.

deepDive.heading: HVAC estimates: load calculation, equipment sizing and the rebate paperwork
deepDive.sub: An HVAC estimate that is really a equipment quote invites the wrong comparison — the customer shops the box, not the system. These are the parts that make an HVAC estimate defensible.

blocks.h3: Size the equipment with a load calculation, not by matching the old unit
paras: Replacing a 3-ton unit with another 3-ton unit is the single most common HVAC estimating error. The original may have been oversized for the ductwork, the windows may have been replaced since, and the house may have had insulation added. A Manual J load calculation takes an hour and produces the tonnage the house actually needs.

State on the estimate that the equipment was sized by load calculation, and include the targets: sensible and latent load, design temperatures, and the resulting tonnage. Customers who receive two quotes rarely know how to compare them — this is the line that shows your number was calculated and theirs was guessed.
list: Manual J load calculation summary attached or referenced
Whether existing ductwork can carry that airflow

blocks.h3: Efficiency ratings, rebates and the 25C tax credit
paras: Equipment efficiency is now a selling document as much as a technical one. SEER2 ratings took effect in 2023, and the minimums differ by region, so a unit that is legal in one state may not be installable in another. The estimate should state the SEER2 and HSPF2 of the proposed equipment and the regional minimum it meets.

Rebates and federal credits change yearly and are frequently the reason a customer chooses the higher-efficiency unit. If you are going to mention them, state the amount, the eligibility conditions and that the customer is responsible for claiming it. An estimate that promises a rebate the customer then fails to qualify for becomes a discount you gave away.

The three regions exist because the old single national minimum was replaced in 2023 by regional ones tied to climate. Always check the current map before quoting equipment, and note the rating on the estimate: a customer comparing two bids on price alone is usually comparing different efficiency classes without knowing it.

blocks.h3: The system is more than the box: line set, ductwork and commissioning
paras: An equipment-only quote leaves out the parts that determine whether the system works: the line set and its length, the pad or bracket, the disconnect, the condensate management, the thermostat, and any duct modifications the new airflow requires. Each is a real cost that a competitor's lower bid may simply not include.

Commissioning is the last piece. A professional installation includes measuring static pressure, verifying charge by subcooling or superheat, and documenting airflow. Put that on the estimate as an included line — it is cheap for you to do and expensive for the customer to discover was skipped.
list: Line set length and routing, including any required relocation
Pad/bracket, disconnect, whip, condensate pump or trap
Duct modifications for the new airflow
Commissioning: static pressure, charge verification, airflow measurement

blocks.h3: Warranty structure and the maintenance that keeps it valid
paras: Manufacturer warranties on HVAC equipment are typically five to ten years on parts and twenty on the heat exchanger for residential, but they are conditional. Registration within a window, annual maintenance records, and proof of licensed installation are common conditions — and customers discover them when a compressor fails in year four.

The estimate should state your labour warranty separately from the manufacturer's parts warranty, and name the maintenance requirement that keeps both valid. Offering a maintenance plan as an optional line converts a warranty condition into recurring revenue, which is why most HVAC companies push it at the point of sale.
list: Manufacturer parts warranty term and registration requirement
Maintenance required to keep the warranty valid
Maintenance plan offered as an optional annual line
